script.quote: The MINIVAC is so programmed that the machine will move 5 squares to the right of its own last move if and only if the human opponent has blocked that last move by moving 4 squares to the right of the machine's last move. If the human player did not move 4 squares to the right of the machine's last move, MINIVAC will move into that square and indicate a win. / The play continues as above until either light 1 comes on—indicating that MINIVAC wins; or light 2 comes on—indicating a tie.

note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A): every expect and until is derived by hand from the 70 jack-to-jack wires plus the two free play wires and the p.55 rule, not printed. Corpus tier D: smoke plus the stated invariant (plan Step 7). No erratum changes a wire; ER-44 is prose and is honoured at the fifth move. Play wires are cords 70 (machine, M10#3) and 71 (player, M11#3) as in C2/VI-TICTACTOE; the free end goes in 6com#2, M9b#2 or Mnb#2 / Mnt#2 (hole #1 holds the program wire). Topology settles the 'squares to the right' direction: the relay 3-6 contact tree reaches D(n+5) and D(n+4) in panel numbering, which is FALLBACK-TTT-RING-CW (4 to the right is direction-free; 5 to the right is +5 mod 8). After the centre the machine replies one square to the right of the player (N-1), derived, not printed. Script choices, not printed: player squares (game 1: 1, 6, 3, 8 tie; game 2: 1, 5 loses at move 3; game 3: 1, 6, 3, 5 loses at move 5), pushbutton 6 pressed 300 ms before the move button, 2 s settle after each stop, pb1 released before pb6. Start dial D0 is the construction state. Relay 1 and relays 3-6 race at each pushbutton 6 press (relay 3-6 feed runs through relay 1 N.C.); only settled states are asserted. Rotary run rate and coast are profile fallbacks.
